selection.reason: Exercise credential-independent publication, evidence authenticity, CI admission and concurrent remote updates through generated synthetic repositories. Capture genuine assertion failure before implementation and complete passing categories afterward. Preserve original execution history and delivery clocks; retain independently applicable unchanged observations. No automatic recurrence expansion or paid fallback.

spec.title: SSH publication with verifiable native validation
acceptance: A generated repository can export evidence without invoking an authenticated CLI. Export verifies the local source commit and tree, constructs a reproducible evidence object using fixed synthetic metadata, includes exactly one regular validation.json blob and exactly one source parent, and binds the envelope bytes through the commit message digest. The dedicated evidence ref is updated with an explicit observed-value lease and its resulting object identity is checked remotely.

A fresh checkout imports evidence through Git without REST access when the repository owner identifier is available from the CI environment. Import checks the source parent and tree, sole blob entry, envelope size, digest and reproducible commit identity before applying the existing strict repository, issuer and command-contract checks. Missing, malformed, oversized, redirected or altered evidence contributes no imported coverage, and release validation executes all uncovered commands.

Public HTTP reads use an HTTPS GitHub API destination, accept GET only, attach no credentials, bound response size and request duration, and reject unsuccessful or malformed responses. CI admission retains repository, source, workflow, event, attempt and unique required-job verification; incomplete or unsuccessful observations cannot produce a prepared publication.

CI admission examines compatible existing runs before creating a watched branch. Branch inspection uses exact Git ref discovery, creation requires an absent-ref lease, and a conflicting concurrent update is refused. An unavailable authenticated retry reports the affected run and manual recovery action while preserving the original failure and issuing no publication descriptor.

Publication uses the prepared source and destination with an explicit lease against the captured remote object, using an empty expectation for an absent destination. Tests advance the remote between preparation and publication, including an update that ordinary fast-forward checks would allow, and prove refusal without changing the remote. Existing preparation ancestry checks, immutable tuple verification, approval decisions and native hook admission remain effective.

Transport preserves the existing envelope schema, sanitized execution metadata, complete command identities and original provenance. Export still requires independently approved source coverage; corrupted originals and unsupported historical qualification remain rejected. Required CI success remains bound to the exact source even when imported command coverage is unavailable.

The revised sealed contract binds the planned runtime paths and exact selected modules. The focused module records a complete assertion failure on the unchanged implementation and passes afterward with identical reproduction inputs; all selected categories finish without skipped or incomplete cases, and prior execution outcomes remain intact.

Maintained workflow instructions agree across both client copies and describe Git evidence transport, unauthenticated reads, failed-run recovery and leased publication. SSH credential selection remains local configuration, introduces no versioned secret or sibling-project dependency, and preserves the read-only CI credential boundary and separate protected-effect admission.

tests.purpose: Reproduce credential-dependent transport and missing lease behavior, then verify real Git evidence exchange, tamper rejection, public reads and concurrent-update refusal.
Verify strict envelope custody, native execution provenance, complete fallback coverage and CI identity and recovery checks.
Verify prepared publication identity, approval admission, transport ordering, remote leases and unchanged bounded hook behavior.
Verify release admission, package boundaries and execution of commands lacking valid imported evidence.
Verify revised contract binding, genuine reproduction, selected-category completeness and retained original execution records.

findings.message: Accepting validation attestations from repository writers changes issuer authority. Activation requires exact owner authority for that writer set; technical approval supplies none. Repository and owner hashes identify scope and do not authenticate the individual writer.
